youtube.title: The Radium Girls: Told It Was Safe, They Sued and Changed the Law
youtube.description:
In the late 1910s, young women painting glowing watch dials in Orange, New Jersey were taught to shape their brushes with their lips: lip, dip, paint. They were told the radium paint was harmless. Their jaws crumbled. Their bones turned radioactive. Then five of them sued. This is the full file: the hidden report, the bones that gave the secret away, and the courtroom where the women were too sick to raise their hands.
